propositions.name: elastic_medium_carries_light
propositions.quote: the optical hypothesis of an elastic medium through which the vibrations of light are propagated
propositions.statement: Light is propagated as vibrations through an elastic medium.

propositions.name: field_has_definite_equations
propositions.quote: we arrived at certain equations expressing certain properties of the electromagnetic field
propositions.statement: The electromagnetic field has certain properties that can be expressed by certain equations.

propositions.name: field_properties_may_explain_light
propositions.quote: these properties of that which constitutes the electromagnetic field, deduced from electromagnetic phenomena alone, are sufficient to explain the propagation of light through the same substance
propositions.statement: The properties of the electromagnetic field, deduced from electromagnetic phenomena alone, are sufficient to explain the propagation of light through the same substance.

propositions.name: magnetization_confined_to_wave_plane
propositions.quote: which shows that the direction of the magnetization must be in the plane of the wave.
propositions.statement: The direction of the magnetization must be in the plane of the wave.

propositions.name: perfect_dielectric_has_no_conduction
propositions.quote: If the medium in the field is a perfect dielectric there is no true conduction, and the currents
propositions.statement: If the medium in the field is a perfect dielectric there is no true conduction.

propositions.name: displacements_caused_by_electromotive_force
propositions.quote: But these electric displacements are caused by electromotive forces, and by the equations of Electric Elasticity (E),
propositions.statement: Electric displacements are caused by electromotive forces.

propositions.name: electromotive_force_from_field_variation
propositions.quote: These electromotive forces are due to the variations either of the electromagnetic or the electrostatic functions, as there is no motion of conductors in the field
propositions.statement: Electromotive forces are due to the variations either of the electromagnetic or the electrostatic functions, as there is no motion of conductors in the field.

propositions.name: wave_propagates_bidirectionally_same_speed
propositions.quote: The other equations give the same value for V, so that the wave is propagated in either direction with a velocity V.
propositions.statement: The wave is propagated in either direction with a velocity V.

propositions.name: wave_entirely_magnetic
propositions.quote: This wave consists entirely of magnetic disturbances, the direction of magnetization being in the plane of the wave.
propositions.statement: This wave consists entirely of magnetic disturbances, the direction of magnetization being in the plane of the wave.

propositions.name: no_nontransverse_magnetic_wave
propositions.quote: No magnetic disturbance whose direction of magnetization is not in the plane of the wave can be propagated as a plane wave at all.
propositions.statement: No magnetic disturbance whose direction of magnetization is not in the plane of the wave can be propagated as a plane wave at all.

propositions.name: magnetic_disturbance_transverse_like_light
propositions.quote: Hence magnetic disturbances propagated through the electromagnetic field agree with light in this, that the disturbance at any point is transverse to the direction of propagation, and such waves may have all the properties of polarized light.
propositions.statement: Magnetic disturbances propagated through the electromagnetic field agree with light in that the disturbance at any point is transverse to the direction of propagation, and such waves may have all the properties of polarized light.

propositions.name: v_equals_ratio_and_should_equal_light_velocity
propositions.quote: is the number of electrostatic units in one electromagnetic unit of electricity, and this, according to our result, should be equal to the velocity of light in air or vacuum.
propositions.statement: v, the number of electrostatic units in one electromagnetic unit of electricity, should be equal to the velocity of light in air or vacuum.

propositions.name: fizeau_measured_light_velocity
propositions.quote: The velocity of light in air, by M. Fizeau 's experiments, is
propositions.statement: The velocity of light in air was measured by Fizeau's experiments.

propositions.name: aberration_measured_light_velocity
propositions.quote: The velocity of light in the space surrounding the earth, deduced from the coefficient of aberration and the received value of the radius of the earth's orbit, is
propositions.statement: The velocity of light in the space surrounding the earth is deduced from the coefficient of aberration and the received value of the radius of the earth's orbit.

propositions.name: light_and_magnetism_same_substance
propositions.quote: The agreement of the results seems to show that light and magnetism are affections of the same substance, and that light is an electromagnetic disturbance propagated through the field according to electromagnetic laws.
propositions.statement: The agreement of the results seems to show that light and magnetism are affections of the same substance, and that light is an electromagnetic disturbance propagated through the field according to electromagnetic laws.

propositions.name: no_wave_depends_on_j
propositions.quote: and the value of J is either constant or zero, or uniformly increasing or diminishing with the time; so that no disturbance depending on J can be propagated as a wave.
propositions.statement: The value of J is either constant or zero, or uniformly increasing or diminishing with the time, so that no disturbance depending on J can be propagated as a wave.

propositions.name: equations_show_transversal_only
propositions.quote: The equations of the electromagnetic field, deduced from purely experimental evidence, show that transversal vibrations only can be propagated.
propositions.statement: The equations of the electromagnetic field, deduced from purely experimental evidence, show that transversal vibrations only can be propagated.

propositions.name: no_evidence_of_electric_density
propositions.quote: We have, however, no evidence as to the density of electricity, as we do not even know whether to consider vitreous electricity as a substance or as the absence of a substance.
propositions.statement: There is no evidence as to the density of electricity, and it is not known whether to consider vitreous electricity as a substance or as the absence of a substance.

propositions.name: both_sciences_affirm_transverse_only
propositions.quote: Hence electromagnetic science leads to exactly the same conclusions as optical science with respect to the direction of the disturbances which can be propagated through the field; both affirm the propagation of transverse vibrations
propositions.statement: Electromagnetic science leads to exactly the same conclusions as optical science with respect to the direction of the disturbances which can be propagated through the field; both affirm the propagation of transverse vibrations.

propositions.name: inductive_capacity_equals_refraction_squared_over_mu
propositions.quote: the Specific Inductive Capacity is equal to the square of the index of refraction divided by the coefficient of magnetic induction.
propositions.statement: The Specific Inductive Capacity is equal to the square of the index of refraction divided by the coefficient of magnetic induction.

propositions.name: crystal_axes_assumption
propositions.quote: we shall assume that the axes of magnetic induction coincide in direction with those of electric elasticity.
propositions.statement: In a crystallized medium the axes of magnetic induction coincide in direction with those of electric elasticity.

propositions.name: principal_plane_ordinary_refraction
propositions.quote: Now we know that in each principal plane of a crystal the ray polarized in that plane obeys the ordinary law of refraction, and therefore its velocity is the same in whatever direction in that plane it is propagated.
propositions.statement: In each principal plane of a crystal the ray polarized in that plane obeys the ordinary law of refraction, and its velocity is the same in whatever direction in that plane it is propagated.

propositions.name: crystals_show_unequal_magnetic_coefficients
propositions.quote: We know, from the magnetic experiments of Faraday , Plucker , &c, that in many crystals
propositions.statement: From the magnetic experiments of Faraday and Plucker, in many crystals the magnetic coefficients are unequal.

propositions.name: knoblauch_crystal_induction_experiments
propositions.quote: The experiments of Knoblauch Magazine on electric induction through crystals seem to show that
propositions.statement: The experiments of Knoblauch on electric induction through crystals seem to show that the electric elasticity coefficients may be different.

propositions.name: crystal_inequality_too_small_for_double_refraction
propositions.quote: is so small that great magnetic forces are required to indicate their difference, and the differences do not seem of sufficient magnitude to account for the double refraction of the crystals.
propositions.statement: The inequality of the magnetic coefficients is so small that great magnetic forces are required to indicate their difference, and the differences do not seem of sufficient magnitude to account for the double refraction of the crystals.

propositions.name: further_crystal_experiments_needed
propositions.quote: Further experiments on the magnetic and dielectric properties of crystals are required before we can decide whether the relation of these bodies to magnetic and electric forces is the same, when these forces are permanent
propositions.statement: Further experiments on the magnetic and dielectric properties of crystals are required before it can be decided whether the relation of these bodies to magnetic and electric forces is the same when the forces are permanent as when they are alternating with the rapidity of the vibrations of light.

propositions.name: conduction_converts_energy_to_heat
propositions.quote: then there will be not only electric displacements, but true currents of conduction in which electrical energy is transformed into heat, and the undulation is thereby weakened.
propositions.statement: In a conductor there are true currents of conduction in which electrical energy is transformed into heat, and the undulation is thereby weakened.

propositions.name: transparent_bodies_are_insulators
propositions.quote: Most transparent solid bodies are good insulators, whereas all good conductors are very opaque.
propositions.statement: Most transparent solid bodies are good insulators, whereas all good conductors are very opaque.

propositions.name: electrolytes_conduct_yet_transparent
propositions.quote: Electrolytes allow a current to pass easily and yet are often very transparent.
propositions.statement: Electrolytes allow a current to pass easily and yet are often very transparent.

propositions.name: incomplete_separation_hypothesis
propositions.quote: We may suppose, however, that in the rapidly alternating vibrations of light, the electromotive forces act for so short a time that they are unable to effect a complete separation between the particles in combination
propositions.statement: In the rapidly alternating vibrations of light, the electromotive forces act for so short a time that they are unable to effect a complete separation between the particles in combination.

propositions.name: thin_metal_plates_transmit_light
propositions.quote: Gold, silver, and platinum are good conductors, and yet when reduced to sufficiently thin plates they allow light to pass through them.
propositions.statement: Gold, silver, and platinum are good conductors, and yet when reduced to sufficiently thin plates they allow light to pass through them.

propositions.name: energy_loss_depends_on_reversal_rate
propositions.quote: This result cannot be reconciled with the electromagnetic theory of light, unless we suppose that there is less loss of energy when the electromotive forces are reversed with the rapidity of the vibrations of light
propositions.statement: This result cannot be reconciled with the electromagnetic theory of light, unless there is less loss of energy when the electromotive forces are reversed with the rapidity of the vibrations of light than when they act for sensible times.

propositions.name: energy_half_magnetic_half_electric
propositions.quote: where P represents the greatest value of the electromotive force. Half of this consists of magnetic and half of electric energy.
propositions.statement: Half of the energy per unit of volume consists of magnetic and half of electric energy.

propositions.name: forces_reversed_at_light_frequency
propositions.quote: These electromotive and magnetic forces must be conceived to be reversed twice in every vibration of light; that is, more than a thousand million million times in a second.
propositions.statement: The electromotive and magnetic forces must be conceived to be reversed twice in every vibration of light, that is, more than a thousand million million times in a second.
